thread:
maria (Acme): hey team, after the VPC migration our app calls to the private service endpoint svc.internal.acme.redwood:443 are failing from prod VPC. getting NXDOMAIN or TLS handshake errors. not seeing this from staging. cc @lena

lena (Support): thanks — can you paste `dig` / `curl` / `openssl` outputs and your prod VPC id? also let us know if you have an egress proxy or allowlist.

maria (Acme): prod VPC is vpc-0a1b2c3d. dig +short from a pod:```
; dig +short svc.internal.acme.redwood
; (no output)
```
curl error from app:```
curl -v https://svc.internal.acme.redwood/health
*   Trying 52.24.12.9...
* Connected to 52.24.12.9 (52.24.12.9) port 443 (#0)
* SSL: handshaking: SSL_connect returned=1 errno=0 state=SSLv3 read server certificate B: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
```
Also tried `kubectl exec` into pod and `dig svc.internal.acme.redwood @10.0.0.2` (node-local) => NXDOMAIN. We do have an egress allowlist for a small set of IPs and use an outbound proxy at 10.1.1.5.

raj (SRE): NXDOMAIN from node-local at 10.0.0.2 suggests the private hosted zone might not be associated with that VPC or the node-local cache has a stale answer. can you paste output of `kubectl exec -n kube-system node-local-dns -- curl -sS http://127.0.0.1:9253/metrics` (just in case) and `cat /etc/resolv.conf` from a node?

dave (Infra): also check for duplicate private hosted zones or wrong assoc after migration. run:```
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name 'internal.acme.redwood'
aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id Z123EXAMPLE
```
Look for VPCs association block. If the prod VPC is missing, that explains NXDOMAIN.

maria (Acme): ran list-hosted-zones-by-name, here's trimmed output:```
{
  "HostedZones": [
    {
      "Id": "/hostedzone/Z9EXAMPLE",
      "Name": "internal.acme.redwood.",
      "Config": {"PrivateZone": true},
      "ResourceRecordSetCount": 5
    }
  ]
}
# get-hosted-zone Z9EXAMPLE shows "VPCs": [] (no associations)
```

lena (Support): that fits. if the private hosted zone is not associated with prod VPC, resolver in that VPC won't answer for the name and will forward to public DNS or your egress proxy. For service endpoints, missing assoc -> unexpected public IPs (and cert mismatch/TLS failures).

raj (SRE): also note the curl showed it hit 52.24.12.9 (public). run:`openssl s_client -connect 52.24.12.9:443 -servername svc.internal.acme.redwood` and paste cert CN/SAN. if cert CN != svc.internal.acme.redwood that's further proof of hitting public endpoint.

maria (Acme): openssl output:```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Amazon, CN = Amazon Root CA 1
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=global-public.acme.example.com
   i:/C=US/O=Amazon/CN=Amazon
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=global-public.acme.example.com
```
Looks like global-public cert, not the internal cert.

dave (Infra): OK. plan: re-associate Z9EXAMPLE with vpc-0a1b2c3d and ensure resolver rules / forwarders are intact. I'll open an infra change, target low-traffic window. @raj can you validate our shared forwarder health (10.12.34.10) and confirm it isn't returning stale records?

raj (SRE): will check forwarder. quick remediation you can do on your side: 1) ensure your egress proxy allows our forwarder IPs 10.12.34.0/24 and 2) flush node-local DNS cache after assoc: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod -l k8s-app=node-local-dns` or restart daemonset so caches clear.

maria (Acme): we'll add the forwarder range to allowlist and plan to flush node-local. will confirm when done.

deploy-bot: Created INFRA-5234 - re-associate hosted zone Z9EXAMPLE -> vpc-0a1b2c3d (assigned to dave)

lena (Support): tagging eng-dns for visibility. once infra assoc is done, run the same `dig` and `openssl` tests and paste results. if issues persist, we'll trace resolver rules and check for duplicate hosted zones across accounts. thanks, everyone.
